message.content: Trade significantly shaped the pharaoh's power in ancient Egypt. It gave him the resources to build monuments, and his scribes ensured that taxes flowed from merchants. We must recognize that the pharaoh controlled every trade route, and his authority extended to the Nile's banks. You can see that without trade, the king's military would have weakened, since he relied on gold, spices, and timber from foreign lands. They—his subjects—paid tribute to him, and their loyalty depended on the wealth that flowed through the ports. The pharaoh's own agents managed these exchanges, and it was their duty to protect the routes. If a foreign nation refused to trade, the pharaoh's prestige would diminish, and his people would question his divine right to rule. He could not ignore the consequences, because his entire kingdom depended on foreign goods. We should not underestimate how trade strengthened the pharaoh's grip on power; it was truly the foundation of his rule, and without it, the entire system would have collapsed.
